tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__cua_repl
tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

completion_summary.description: Write a headline for the observed outcome in three to six words total. Start with a past-tense verb and name the result in plain language, as in 'Booked a plumber for Thursday' or 'Renewed vehicle registration'. Leave identifiers, values, and explanations for the reply.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
</app-context>

# FORGE v4 — General-purpose Super-agent

The desktop frontend now has a six-stage Codex-style refactor, with a single
260px sidebar, inline Worker runs and UI paths for the current 50 authenticated
API routes. See the [frontend acceptance report](desktop/CODEX-REFACTOR-REPORT.md),
[API-to-UI map](desktop/API-UI-COVERAGE.md) and [desktop instructions](desktop/README.md).

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose DeepSeek-style Super-agent desktop
application: one persistent Router conversation coordinates hidden, isolated
Workers and continuously receives events.

The current backend capability sprint adds project-focused context, bounded
specialist dependencies and expansion, real CPython unittest execution, model
microbenchmarks and progress-based stall detection. Read the
[capability report](docs/SUPERAGENT_CAPABILITY_SPRINT_REPORT.md) and
[experiment record](docs/SUPERAGENT_EXPERIMENTS.md) for current acceptance and
limitations. No frontend redesign or external Agent execution backend is added.
Current full capability acceptance has **not passed**: real L1 and single-Worker
L2 tasks passed; the final multi-specialist L2 and L3 condition stopped before
delivery. Correct two-project task association, distinct-task parallel Workers,
Thread pass-through and bounded relationship Recall were observed. The latest
continuation uses the user's explicit DeepSeek **100M**
model context declaration while retaining conflicting discovery metadata.
Model capacity, request affordability and cumulative spending are separate.
Later targeted probes are not task reacceptance. Exact outcomes and
source hashes are indexed in [final verification](docs/audit/superagent/final-verification.json).

`python_unittest` executes approved Python with the current OS account. It uses
an exact SHA-256 manifest, an R2 approval, a private working directory, a minimal
environment and a ten-second process-tree limit; this is not an OS sandbox.
Changed source requires another exact approval. The existing `python_test`
restricted-function tool remains available separately.

Authenticated model-intelligence APIs provide identity discovery
(`POST /api/model-intelligence/discover`), existing-record performance/health
(`GET /api/model-intelligence/{profile_id}`), and bounded text microprobes
(`POST /api/model-intelligence/benchmark`, with `profile_id` and optional
`dimensions`). Discovery does not establish capability. The six fixed probes
record source, sample size, time, usage and confidence; vision remains unknown.
These endpoints use the configured Provider and existing Registry/benchmark
records. They require no additional dependencies or environment variables.

An optional trusted `FORGE_MODEL_CALL_LIMIT` sets a positive total HTTP-attempt
ceiling for the existing workspace ledger. Settled, rejected, reserved and
unknown attempts all count; restarting Core does not refund attempts. This cap
is independent of model context capacity and cumulative Token/cost ceilings.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. DeepSeek Super-agent defines the overall architecture; Codex and Claude Code inform Harness design. None is an execution backend.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering implementation with bounded context recovery, source-bound
recall and evidence-gated execution. A configured Provider is required; Mock
tests and real Provider observations are identified separately. Autonomous
internal plan/team contracts use an auditable host mandate tied to the original
request or admitted Trigger. Manual approvals retain authenticated user authority,
and risky tool actions still require their own authorization. A mandate or
proposal does not prove execution. Worker directories are private execution
contexts, not an OS sandbox. General complex-task correctness remains subject to
recorded acceptance.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), and `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`.
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` optionally caps the registered model context window.
When omitted, Router uses the Model Registry window. Current local DeepSeek
Provider metadata reports 1000000 input tokens and 128000 output tokens. This capacity is separate from
cumulative task spending limits and is not an independently measured maximum. Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` | Defaults to `false`: cumulative workspace, Quest, team and Worker token estimates do not stop execution. Usage is still recorded and unsettled calls remain unresolved. Set `true` to opt into cumulative limits and configure `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT`. Model context/output limits, concurrency, tool permissions, deadlines and review counts still apply. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE` | Router response-token ceiling and reserved output allowance; integer `1`–`8192`, defaults to `2048`. `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` must be greater than this value. A registered model's known output limit must also support it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` | Operator-supplied Router context ceiling, required when setting a Router model. Core startup requires an integer greater than `2048` and greater than the configured output reserve. |

The Phase 2 live acceptance harness uses a 120-second timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional
Gateway retries, with a Router output reserve of `4096` and `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=3`
within the scenario's three-round cap. Router/Planner schema repair remains a separately bounded stage;
neither setting authorizes replay of an unresolved external action.

The current WorkBuddy acceptance harness explicitly requests `reasoning_effort=none`,
which the local proxy implementation advertises for the requested model. This is
an operator setting, not independent proof of the upstream model's internal behavior.
Earlier diagnostic runs used the proxy default and retain their separate results.

The Router reads a bounded snapshot and calls the provider outside the database write
transaction. A successful decision and its messages commit together; provider errors, invalid
decisions, or budget failures leave no messages or Quest changes for that turn. The caller can
retry with the same request ID. The context budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate,
reserves output and request overhead, and also respects a known registry context window. Tool
access is limited to read-only Core queries. Worker execution separately requires approved plan/team contracts and governed tool permissions.

### Core authentication and development bootstrap

Core requires a fresh cryptographically random 32-byte process secret; `.env` is explicitly rejected. For manual browser development, supply it as 64 hex characters in `FORGE_CORE_SECRET` using a protected input method and enter the same secret into the UI's password field. Never place it in command history, source files, URLs, logs, or persistent browser storage. In the native desktop integration, the parent supplies the secret through a private pipe and the UI receives the derived session bearer in memory. Restarting Core invalidates old bearer tokens. Native integration is still undergoing final verification.

The unauthenticated public loopback `/health` returns only liveness and a random per-process session challenge; an authenticated request also receives Router identity and background status. A trusted client computes the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 challenge using the decoded 32-byte secret, and sends `Authorization: Bearer <digest>` on API requests. Requests without an Origin are allowed only with authentication and a loopback peer and Host; browser requests must also use an explicitly allowed Origin. These boundaries protect against unauthorized webpages and other untrusted clients; they do not protect secrets from an attacker who can read the same OS user's process memory. Keep the development server and any allowed origin trusted.

The authenticated user API supports `POST /api/approvals`, `GET /api/approvals?quest_id=...`, `GET /api/approvals/{id}`, and POSTs to `/{id}/decision` or `/{id}/revoke`. Workspace grants use `GET`/`POST /api/quests/{id}/grants` and `POST /api/quests/{id}/grants/revoke`. Decisions and grants record the authenticated local user, not a caller-supplied actor. The bearer represents that user; it must never be exposed to a model or registered as an Agent tool. These routes do not execute actions or accept trusted evidence. The M7 desktop approval and scope controls are under integration testing.

### Workspace and Settings

`python -m forge_api` is the shared Core launcher. From the repository root on Windows, `./scripts/run-backend.ps1` sets up the virtual environment and uses that launcher without shell activation. Pass `-WorkspaceRoot 'D:\YourWorkspace'` to the script, or `python -m forge_api --workspace-root 'D:\YourWorkspace'` directly. Workspace roots must be absolute paths.

The CLI launcher supervises a separate Core process and restarts unexpected exits
with bounded backoff (at most five restarts in ten minutes; five minutes of stable
operation resets that count). Normal shutdown, invalid configuration and a restore
fence stop recovery. A separate supervisor lock prevents duplicate launchers, and
the Core retains its existing Workspace lock. The bootstrap secret reaches the
child through a private pipe; each replacement rotates its session challenge and
invalidates old bearer tokens. On Windows a Job Object drains the Core's descendant
processes before recovery and kills them if the supervisor dies. The native
`--desktop-host` protocol is unchanged; automatic native desktop process restart
is not yet integrated.

The default Workspace is independent of the checkout, installation and shell directory:

| OS | Default Workspace root |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| Linux | `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/forge/workspaces/default` |

convergence, complete multi-specialist/L3 acceptance and long-duration recovery.
The small samples establish no best team or model-routing algorithm.

## Closed continuation and active repairs

The next fixed phase is closed with its 338-file freeze unchanged. Explicit user
metadata selects DeepSeek's 100M context; discovered 1M metadata is retained as
a conflict. Request affordability, complete native framing reservations and
cumulative spending remain separate constraints. The inherited handoff is now
included before choosing a compaction tail, avoiding a false preparation refusal.

Real L1 `20261115T231549Z-capability-project-4348f1` passed all gates (13 calls,
161807 tokens); single L2 `20261115T231841Z-capability-single-db92c8` also passed
(13 calls, 154299 tokens). Both performed actual file/tool work, a real Reviewer
revision followed by PASS, independent citation checks and reviewed completion
back to the original Router. These establish bounded task outcomes only.

Continuity failed on two Router `json_invalid` responses before task admission;
raw responses were not retained, so their exact syntax cause is unknown. Fixed
L2 stalled after repairs=4/4 without converging its `review_pending` state, and
Watchdog help was rejected by Dispatcher for missing protocol fields. An
explicitly injected HTTP503 triggered native DeepSeek-to-GLM replacement with
the rejection's full reservation retained, but the fallback directory operation
became uncertain and the task failed. It must not be replayed.

This phase has 50 attempts: 49 real upstream calls settled, one injected
rejection was not forwarded, 515841 known tokens, one rejection with unknown
usage and one unknown tool outcome. See [immutable phase closure](audit/superagent/capability-continuation-closure.json).
Full backend regression recorded **2652 passed, 14 failed, 3 skipped**. Thirteen
failures match the previous stage; the additional test incorrectly compares
model context capacity with cumulative balance. A read-only diagnosis checks
actual reservations instead and passes; the original failure remains recorded.
The following corrections were implemented on the intermediate 342-file freeze.
Its real task reports and full regression are closed in the repair-phase record;
the 345-file final outcome above is authoritative. The following sections
describe the earlier phase.

The recovery correction binds the exact current settled independent review,
packet, approved plan/team and generation before atomically converging an
exhausted revision to `blocked`. It recovers an existing revision-blocked marker
after restart, and preserves unknown-effect fences and every original counter.
Watchdog now supplies the strict v2 help fields; actual Dispatcher inbox delivery
is tested without granting expert expansion. Recovery tests: 213 passed.

`directory_create` accepts a precreated authorized ordinary directory after
checking the original path, every parent and reparse/link status. It never
replays an existing uncertain intent. Related tool/security/runtime tests:
131 passed, two old Windows environment skips. The first-archive test now checks
actual reservations against remaining spending, while requiring the true model
window to remain unchanged.

Router requests use a wire-only strict schema with all advertised properties
required; local Pydantic defaults, nullable types and validators are unchanged.
Only a complete exact lowercase LF JSON fence can be stripped as a separately
audited transport wrapper. No substring extraction, syntax repair or extra
reflection is added. Raw and normalized hashes and safe syntax-position metadata
are retained without response excerpts. This does not explain the earlier
unretained malformed response or prove Provider strict JSON conformance. Router
joint tests: 264 passed; these overlap other suites and must not be added.

## Audit before implementation

The starting checkout was clean. README, STATUS, implementation report, source
and the preserved acceptance index were read first. STATUS still led with older
Phase 2 results; the actual baseline is the newer Super-agent implementation:
2312 passing tests, fourteen reproduced historical failures, two Windows skips,
and two bounded real scenarios with 39 settled calls. These historical successes
do not establish the more complex L1/L2/L3 required here.

Existing Worker inference/tools/checkpoints, DAG dependencies, source-verified
predecessor deliveries, partial replanning, model observations, Wilson intervals,
Registry discovery, compaction and governance are reused. Targeted starting
regression passed **104 tests** in `audit/superagent/capability-baseline.xml`.

| Sprint | Actual gap | Minimum change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Router context ignores project links; ambiguity spans projects; lifecycle controls stay outside conversation | Project-focused retrieval/candidates, source-bound project selection, coordination facts and conversational controls; same Router/CAS |
| B | Python tools cannot execute stdlib project tests; failed executable test result has no safe repair proof | Exact-manifest R2 CPython unittest tool, private cwd, process-tree cleanup, consumed approval proof and existing bounded repair loop |
| C | Autonomous contracts forbid dependencies although scheduler already supports them | Bounded coarse expert topology, verified handoffs, role-specific tools, source-bound help and bounded replacement/expansion |
| D | Identity discovery is not capability measurement; some health/outcome projections are absent | Extend existing performance projection and benchmark_runs with small attributed probes; keep unsupported dimensions unknown |
| E | Task-centric project isolation and long-term object retrieval need stronger tests | Project-filtered source retrieval and multi-hop/compaction continuity on existing records, preserving hashes and revocation |
| F | Healthy loop heartbeat does not establish Worker progress | Inspect actual checkpoints/settlements, emit deduplicated help with source references; retain lease/unknown-effect fences |
| G | Earlier live tasks were bounded file markers, not complex content/coding acceptance | New L1/L2/L3 with independent artifact checks and controlled strategy comparisons |

## Validation plan fixed before live execution

Real Provider runs use fresh isolated storage, the already authorized local proxy,
process-environment credentials and the registered Provider context declaration. The initial conservative 65536 profile is superseded by the operator correction and actual 1M API declaration retained in the experiment record. Router output reserve remains 4096. Operator configuration is not edited. Each task keeps the
existing **32-call / 500000-token / 900-second** ceiling; no automatic Gateway
retry is added. A failed or uncertain run is retained and never replayed.

The planned task set is L1 project diagnosis, L2 source-based Agent-framework
research and L3 a small Python feature verified by real tests and independent
held-out cases. L2 also supplies a controlled single-Worker and fixed-team
comparison to the adaptive path: five task runs, at most 160 calls and 2500000
tokens in aggregate. Up to two discovered models may receive one six-dimension
microprobe suite each, separately capped at 16 calls / 100000 tokens. Unknown
prices remain unknown. Small samples support exploratory observations only.

One combined scenario must observe two distinct local project roots, concurrent
Workers, direct Thread follow-up, settled-boundary Core restart, actual context
compaction, typed Recall and delivery to the original Router. A model's claims,
mock fixtures and programmatic checks are recorded separately. Approved Python
code runs with the same OS account; private directories and fixed invocation do
not constitute an OS sandbox or a tamper-proof correctness oracle.

The bounded experiment ceiling includes failed attempts and targeted diagnostic
calls. Final evidence and unresolved limitations below do not predeclare success.

## Implemented changes

Router project focus now filters task candidates, lexical/semantic memory,
recent messages, events, evidence, constraints, archive prose and object/source
readback. Explicit cross-project requests can traverse the shared historical
conversation. Task and project associations remain references, never filesystem
grants. Continuations inherit the target task's authoritative project identity.
Conversation lifecycle controls share the existing Router transaction, CAS and
durable Worker commands; they cannot grant tools or clear unknown effects.

The autonomous v2 mandate uses existing graph/team scheduling for single,
parallel, sequential and hierarchical expert topologies. Completed predecessor
deliveries require the original source/evidence proofs. A single Worker may
request two specialists and an integrator within four cumulative Workers and
depth one. Expansion and replacement preserve spent/unknown budget reservations,
prior outcomes and the original tool/deadline limits. Legacy mandates retain
their original policy and tool scope. Replacement is not counted as expansion.

The CPython tool supports imports, classes and stdlib unittest, with exact-file
authorization, bounded output/time and process-tree cleanup. Known settled test
failures can enter the existing two-repair loop only with matching consumed R2
approval, policy, result protocol and manifest proofs. Timeouts and unknown
external effects remain blocked against replay. Independent held-out tests are
separate host checks; model-written tests are not a trusted correctness oracle.

Model measurements extend existing observations and benchmark_runs rather than
adding another state store. Transport health distinguishes known in-flight work
from unknown attempts. The Watchdog observes transcript/tool/model settlements
and capsule frontiers separately from heartbeats. An unchanged frontier emits a
source-bound, durably deduplicated help event, retaining lease and unknown-effect
fences. A stall observation is not proof of failed task quality or permission to
repeat an external operation.

## Real model microprobes

The retained `20261115T205519Z-capability-model-probes.json` records twelve real
calls, all settled, 1,414 charged tokens and unknown monetary cost. The configured
proxy reported DeepSeek and GLM identities; their upstream identity is unverified.
DeepSeek passed five of six fixed cases; GLM passed three. Each dimension has one
sample, and the exact-response contract also measures format compliance. Research
failed the strict oracle on both; GLM coding and planning responses failed the
JSON contract. Design checks a textual accessibility specification, not image
quality. Vision was unsupported and generated no call. These results do not
establish general capability scores or justify a preferred routing algorithm.

## Observed real-task results

L1 independently passed in `20261115T215924Z-capability-adaptive-45f4e4`:
one real Worker read the actual FORGE modules, wrote its analysis, passed the
model Reviewer and strict source/hash/line/quote checking. The combined run
remained failed because L2 Router admission failed. Earlier L1 attempts and
their inaccurate citation ranges remain failures.

L2 did not complete. A fixed Research → Architect condition admitted the correct
chain but its first Worker blocked after two Reviewer revisions. A subsequent
adaptive condition actually admitted Research and Architect in parallel, with
a dependent Reviewer integrator. Research passed, Architect blocked, and the
integrator never started. The absence of intermediate JSON artifact bodies
from a delivery-only review packet caused blind revisions in the fixed run;
the implementation now projects only source-verified own JSON artifacts into
that review. This fix retains original criteria, scopes and byte limits.

L3 in `20261115T221734Z-capability-continuity-300fa0` produced real code, ran
approved CPython tests, corrected an observed failure, passed the real Reviewer
and all seven independent host holdouts. It still failed full delivery
acceptance: the report cited inferred action names instead of actual test
receipt IDs. The Runtime exposed only the test output, omitting the Core receipt
identity, so the Worker could not cite the ID the checker required. This is a
Harness defect; the checker correctly rejected the report. The subsequent fix
exposes a source-bound Core receipt envelope for Python results and failed-test
feedback. It does not alter old artifacts, receipts or the failed verdict.

The final combined run observed three overlapping Worker ownership intervals
across two tasks, both Thread pass-through paths, a safe Core restart using the
same Router/Worker IDs, compaction of five real Router messages, and typed Recall
references to tasks, Workers, receipts and archives. Recall remained incomplete
at its fixed bounds. These are partial continuity observations. Both tasks were
wrongly linked to the same project, and the final reviewed completion notice
did not reach the Router. An earlier Worker claim did reach the original main
conversation; it must not be reported as the final reviewed completion.

Independent read-only supplements retain these distinctions and source hashes.
The original combined report remains failed. An approval notice exhausted its
bounded processing attempts; the final completion notice remained unprocessed
after four failures. The fixed forty-call admission ceiling blocked further
admissions. No uncertain effects were replayed, and the limit is not a Provider
outage or proof of failed model transport.

## Verification boundary and remaining work

The full `capability-backend-frozen.xml` run recorded **2533 passed, 14 failed,
3 skipped** before the last narrow fixes. Thirteen failures exactly match the
historical baseline; one was an intentional new diagnostic-event contract
conflicting with the older assertion that an invalid Router response leaves no
events. The former historical compact-prompt failure passed after redundant
wording was reduced. The atomicity regression now explicitly verifies unchanged
Router state, no messages/Quests and exactly the safe diagnostic events; it does
not permit scheduling or user-turn side effects. Original failed XMLs are kept.

Later targeted regressions cover the team error hints, receipt visibility,
specialist review, per-task/final accounting and the optional atomic HTTP-attempt
ceiling. See `final-verification.json` for final source hashes and exact suite
counts. Overlapping targeted counts must not be summed as a full suite.

The final full regression on the final production source recorded **2587 passed,
13 failed, 3 skipped**, one existing Starlette deprecation warning, in 556.83
seconds (`capability-backend-final.xml`). All thirteen failures match historical
baseline cases; there are no new failed cases. The diagnostic-event contract
test passes. One already collected project test later received only an import
spacing/unused-variable lint cleanup, and its eleven cases were rerun and passed.
All 59 modified/new Python files pass Ruff; backend/README/docs diff checks pass.
This regression result does not turn the failed live acceptance into a pass.

The final two real Provider probes both recovered exact Python test receipt IDs,
execution states and candidate hashes from the corrected projection. They use
the original historical database read-only and execute no old Worker or test.
Task/diagnostic use totals 160 admitted calls, 159 settled and one old reserved
attempt with unknown outcome; known usage is 1355207 Token. The separate twelve
microprobe calls used 1414 Token. Monetary cost remains unknown. No further real
calls are made beyond the fixed ceiling.

The model window defaults to the Registry declaration. Cumulative allocation,
request affordability, compaction protocol and evidence limits remain separate
checks. `context_budget` was historically a broad external error code, so it
cannot establish that a Provider's declared context window was exhausted.

Unfinished acceptance includes a successful multi-specialist L2, a full L3
delivery after the receipt-envelope fix, correct two-project associations across
the complete live scenario, final reviewed Router notifications and recap, and
a controlled successful single/fixed/dynamic comparison on frozen source.
Dynamic expansion, replacement, failover and stall recovery have targeted
programmatic/scripted coverage; this experiment set does not establish their
live long-term success rates. No superior policy or general capability ranking
is claimed. Tools retain their existing governance; arbitrary shell execution,
OS sandboxing and unrestricted package installation are not introduced.
"}}}

    def _repair_write_scope(self, run_id, token, call):
        """Offer existing grant paths after a proven local pre-execution denial."""
        if type(self.tools) is not ToolEngine:
            return False
        with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
            self._fenced(work.connection, run_id, token)
            feedback = local_write_rejection_feedback(work.connection, run_id, call)
        if feedback is None:
            return False
        return self._repair(
            run_id,
            token,
            reason_code="tool_write_scope_rejected",
            detail=feedback,
            failed_call=call,
            result={
                "state": "rejected_before_execution",
                "call_id": call["call_id"],
                "receipt_id": None,
                "output": feedback,
            },
            preexecution=True,
        )

    def _repair(
        self,
        run_id,
        token,
        *,
        reason_code,
        detail,
        echo=None,
        failed_call=None,
        result=None,
        preexecution=False,
    ):
        """Bounded Worker self-repair: feed the failure back and try once more.

        Returns False when the repair budget or the step budget is spent, in which
        case the caller keeps the existing fail-closed behaviour. An uncertain
        external effect is never replayed by a repair.
        """
        with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
            row = self._fenced(work.connection, run_id, token)
            if row["repairs"] >= self.max_repairs or row["steps"] >= row["step_limit"]:
                return False
            from .worker_envelope import capacity_policy, cycle_allowance

            capsule = json.loads(
                work.connection.execute(
                    "SELECT capsule_json FROM worker_capsules WHERE run_id=?", (run_id,)
                ).fetchone()[0]
            )
            envelope = capacity_policy(capsule)
            remaining_attempts = min(
                self.max_repairs - row["repairs"] - 1,
                row["step_limit"] - row["steps"] - 1,
            )
            if envelope:
                try:
                    remaining_corrections = cycle_allowance(work.connection, row, envelope)[
                        "correction_calls_remaining"
                    ]
                except DomainError:
                    return False
                if not remaining_corrections:
                    return False
                remaining_attempts = min(remaining_attempts, remaining_corrections - 1)
            instruction = (
                "The previous step did not satisfy the task contract. Diagnose "
                "the failure, change your approach, and return JSON that matches "
                "output_schema. Do not repeat the same failing call."
            )
            if envelope:
                instruction += (
                    f" Complete delivery must fit {envelope['max_delivery_bytes']} canonical "
                    "JSON UTF-8 bytes, including all keys, escaping and multibyte characters; "
                    "the output-token allowance does not enlarge that byte bound. "
                    "State required conclusions once and use one shared citation list."
                )
                if not remaining_attempts:
                    instruction += " This is the last approved correction call."
            from .worker_task_sources import CORE_PREFETCH_POLICY

            if capsule.get("input_acquisition_policy") == CORE_PREFETCH_POLICY:
                instruction += (
                    " Reuse the complete Core declared source block and its receipt/hash references. "
                    "Do not repeat those reads; additional observations still require source capacity."
                )
            repair_request = {
                "reason_code": reason_code,
                "detail": detail,
                "attempt": row["repairs"] + 1,
                "remaining_attempts": remaining_attempts,
                "instruction": instruction,
            }
            if preexecution:
                from .tool_domain import CONTRACTS

                contract = next(
                    (item for item in CONTRACTS if item.name == failed_call["tool_name"]), None
                )
                core_feedback = core_read_rejection_feedback(work.connection, run_id, failed_call)
                core_rejection = (
                    type(self.tools) is ToolEngine
                    and reason_code == "source_read_rejected"
                    and core_feedback is not None
                    and core_feedback == result.get("output")
                )
                if (
                    not isinstance(self.tools, ToolEngine)
                    or (
                        failed_call["tool_name"] in CORE_READ_ONLY_TOOLS
                        and reason_code == "source_read_rejected"
                        and not core_rejection
                    )
                    or (contract is None and not core_rejection)
                    or (
                        not core_rejection
                        and contract.risk != "R0"
                        and not (
                            contract.risk == "R1"
                            and reason_code == "tool_write_scope_rejected"
                            and local_write_rejection_feedback(work.connection, run_id, failed_call)
                            == result.get("output")
                            and result.get("output") is not None
                        )
                    )
                    or work.connection.execute(
                        "SELECT 1 FROM action_intents WHERE call_id=?", (failed_call["call_id"],)
                    ).fetchone()
                ):
                    return False
            if failed_call is not None:
                work.connection.execute(
                    "UPDATE worker_tool_calls SET state='failed',receipt_id=?,result_json=? "
                    "WHERE run_id=? AND call_id=? AND state='running'",
                    (result.get("receipt_id"), _json(result), run_id, failed_call["call_id"]),
                )
                checked = work.connection.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM worker_tool_calls WHERE run_id=? AND call_id=?",
                    (run_id, failed_call["call_id"]),
                ).fetchone()
                if not preexecution and not settled_read_failure(
                    work.connection, run_id, checked, require_repair=False
                ):
                    return False
            ordinal = work.connection.execute(
                "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(ordinal),-1)+1 FROM worker_messages WHERE run_id=?", (run_id,)
            ).fetchone()[0]
            if failed_call is not None:
                feedback = {
                    "role": "tool",
                    "tool_call_id": failed_call["model_call_id"],
                    "content": _json(
                        {
                            "state": result["state"],
                            "output": _worker_tool_output(
                                work.connection, row, failed_call, result
                            ),
                            "repair_request": {
                                **repair_request,
                                "instruction": instruction
                                + " Use this diagnostic to choose a corrected new call within the original scope; do not replay the failed call.",
                            },
                        }
                    ),
                }
                work.connection.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO worker_messages VALUES (?,?,'tool',?)",
                    (run_id, ordinal, _json(feedback)),
                )
                ordinal += 1
            if echo:
                work.connection.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO worker_messages VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                    (
                        run_id,
                        ordinal,
                        "assistant",
                        _json({"role": "assistant", "content": echo[:2000]}),
                    ),
                )
                ordinal += 1
            message = {
                "role": "user",
                "content": _json({"repair_request": repair_request}),
            }
            if failed_call is None:
                work.connection.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO worker_messages VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                    (run_id, ordinal, "user", _json(message)),
                )
            work.connection.execute(
                "UPDATE worker_runs SET repairs=repairs+1 WHERE id=?", (run_id,)
            )
            work.connection.execute(
                "UPDATE worker_capsules SET next_action='model',revision=revision+1 WHERE run_id=?",
                (run_id,),
            )
            work.append_event(
                ForgeEvent(
                    event_type="worker.progress",
                    quest_id=row["quest_id"],
                    worker_id=row["worker_id"],
                    payload={
                        "plan_id": row["plan_id"],
                        "task_node_key": row["node_key"],
                        "run_id": run_id,
                        "phase": "self_repair",
                        "correction_reservation_cursor": work.connection.execute(
                            "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(rowid),0) FROM worker_model_reservations WHERE run_id=?",
                            (run_id,),
                        ).fetchone()[0],
                        "reason_code": reason_code,
                        "repair_attempt": row["repairs"] + 1,
                        "failure_category": failure_category(
                            reason_code
                            if preexecution
                            else f"{failed_call['tool_name']}_failed"
                            if failed_call is not None
                            else reason_code
                        ),
                        **(
                            {
                                "failed_call_id": failed_call["call_id"],
                                "receipt_id": result.get("receipt_id"),
                                **(
                                    {
                                        "no_effect": True,
                                        "parameter_digest": parameter_digest(
                                            json.loads(failed_call["arguments_json"])
                                        ),
                                    }
                                    if preexecution
                                    else {}
                                ),
                            }
                    self._fail(
                        run_id,
                        token,
                        "approval_required",
                        call_id=pending["call_id"],
                        call_state="pending",
                    )
                    return self.get(run_id)
                except DomainError as exc:
                    if self._repair_write_scope(run_id, token, pending):
                        continue
                    from .tool_domain import CONTRACTS

                    contract = next(

def narrow_grant(store, worker):
    governance = GovernanceService(store)
    governance.revoke_workspace(worker["quest_id"], "work", "local_user")
    path = "work/" + worker["quest_id"]
    (store.workspace.root / path).mkdir()
    governance.grant_workspace(worker["quest_id"], path, "local_user")
    return path


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["file_write", "directory_create"])
def test_local_write_denial_feeds_real_grant_and_model_chooses_new_path(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, name
):
    store, manager, model, worker = prepared(tmp_path, [], tools=[name])
    root = narrow_grant(store, worker)
    filename = "research.json" if name == "file_write" else "reports"
    values = {"content": '{"observed":true}'} if name == "file_write" else {}
    model.responses[:] = [
        tool(name, {"path": filename, **values}),
        tool(name, {"path": root + "/" + filename, **values}, 2),
        response(delivery()),
    ]
    effects = []
    perform = manager.tools._perform

    def counted(*args):
        effects.append(args[0]["call_id"])
        return perform(*args)

    monkeypatch.setattr(manager.tools, "_perform", counted)
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["repairs"] == 1
    assert len(model.requests) == 3 and len(effects) == 1
    assert not (tmp_path / filename).exists() and (tmp_path / root / filename).exists()
    with store.connection() as c:
        calls = c.execute("SELECT * FROM worker_tool_calls ORDER BY rowid").fetchall()
        assert [call["state"] for call in calls] == ["failed", "succeeded"]
        assert calls[0]["receipt_id"] is None and settled_preexecution_rejection(
            c, worker["id"], calls[0]
        )
        assert not unresolved_calls(c, worker["id"])
        assert c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_intents").fetchone()[0] == 1
        assert c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_receipts").fetchone()[0] == 1
        assert (
            c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM task_grants WHERE revoked_at IS NULL").fetchone()[0]
            == 1
        )
        feedback = json.loads(calls[0]["result_json"])["output"]
        assert feedback["allowed_write_roots"] == [root]
        assert feedback["error_code"] == "local_write_outside_existing_grant"
        receipts, _ = _review_receipts(store, c, c.execute("SELECT * FROM worker_runs").fetchone())
        assert (
            receipts[0]["state"] == "rejected_before_execution"
            and receipts[0]["receipt_id"] is None
        )
    observed = [
        json.loads(item["content"]) for item in model.requests[1].messages if item["role"] == "tool"
    ]
    assert observed[0]["output"]["allowed_write_roots"] == [root]


def test_file_revise_path_rejection_precedes_intent_and_keeps_owned_revision_chain(tmp_path):
    store, manager, model, worker = prepared(tmp_path, [], tools=["file_write", "file_revise"])
    root = narrow_grant(store, worker)
    original = "original"
    model.responses[:] = [
        tool("file_write", {"path": root + "/candidate.py", "content": original}),
        response("placeholder"),
        response("placeholder"),
        response(delivery()),
    ]
    generate = model.generate

    async def choose_revision(request):
        if len(model.requests) in {1, 2}:
            with store.connection() as c:
                receipt = c.execute(
                    "SELECT id FROM action_receipts ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 1"
                ).fetchone()[0]
            number = len(model.requests)
            model.responses[0] = tool(
                "file_revise",
                {
                    "path": "candidate.py" if number == 1 else root + "/candidate.py",
                    "content": "revised",
                    "prior_receipt_id": receipt,
                    "expected_sha256": hashlib.sha256(original.encode()).hexdigest(),
                },
                number + 1,
            )
        return await generate(request)

    model.generate = choose_revision
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["repairs"] == 1
    assert (tmp_path / root / "candidate.py").read_text() == "revised"
    assert not (tmp_path / "candidate.py").exists()
    with store.connection() as c:
        calls = c.execute("SELECT * FROM worker_tool_calls ORDER BY rowid").fetchall()
        assert [call["state"] for call in calls] == ["succeeded", "failed", "succeeded"]
        assert settled_preexecution_rejection(c, worker["id"], calls[1])
        assert c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_intents").fetchone()[0] == 2
        assert c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_receipts").fetchone()[0] == 2

"""Stable private working directories for durable Worker runs, not an OS sandbox."""

import os
import re
import stat
from contextlib import nullcontext
from pathlib import Path

from .domain import DomainError


def worker_environment(store, run_id, *, create=True, connection=None):
    """Resolve only a persisted run; no caller path can select an execution root.

    Directory identity survives a Core restart because workspace, Quest and run
    IDs already persist. Approved shared file operations remain governed by their
    original resource scope; this helper grants no additional filesystem access.
    """
    if not isinstance(run_id, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}", run_id):
        raise DomainError("Invalid Worker environment identity")
    with store.connection() if connection is None else nullcontext(connection) as opened:
        row = opened.execute("SELECT quest_id FROM worker_runs WHERE id=?", (run_id,)).fetchone()
    if row is None or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}", row[0]):
        raise DomainError("Worker environment requires a persisted run")
    quest_id = row[0]
    workspace = Path(store.workspace.root).resolve()
    root = workspace / "data" / "worker-environments" / quest_id / run_id

    def checked_directory(path):
        # Reject links/junctions at every component, before and after creation.
        current = workspace
        for part in path.relative_to(workspace).parts:
            current = current / part
            if create:
                try:
                    current.mkdir(mode=0o700)
                except FileExistsError:
                    pass
            try:
                info = current.lstat()
            except FileNotFoundError:
                if create:
                    raise DomainError("Worker environment directory unavailable") from None
                continue
            if (
                not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode)
                or stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode)
                or getattr(info, "st_file_attributes", 0)
                & getattr(stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT", 0x400)
                or current.resolve() != current
            ):
                raise DomainError("Worker environment cannot use a linked directory")
        return str(path)

    return {
        "version": 1,
        "workspace_id": store.workspace.id,
        "quest_id": quest_id,
        "run_id": run_id,
        "root": checked_directory(root),
        "cwd": checked_directory(root / "work"),
        "tmp": checked_directory(root / "tmp"),
        "output": checked_directory(root / "output"),
        "isolation": "private_working_directory",
        "os_sandbox": False,
    }


def process_environment(base, environment):
    """Use per-run temporary storage without inheriting secrets or a shell home."""
    result = dict(base)
    result.update(TEMP=environment["tmp"], TMP=environment["tmp"], TMPDIR=environment["tmp"])
    if os.name != "nt":
        result["XDG_CACHE_HOME"] = environment["tmp"]
    return result

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "backend" / "scripts"))

import verify_superagent_capability as driver


def enabled_keys(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if value.get("name") == "WB_IN" and value.get("enabled") and not value.get("deleted_at"):
            if isinstance(value.get("key"), str) and value["key"]:
                yield value["key"]
        for item in value.values():
            yield from enabled_keys(item)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for item in value:
            yield from enabled_keys(item)


def main():
    configuration = Path(r"D:\workbuddy2api-hub-v1.8.0\wb-proxy\accounts\settings.json")
    matches = list(enabled_keys(json.loads(configuration.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))))
    if len(matches) != 1:
        raise SystemExit("Exactly one authorized credential is required")
    key = matches[0]
    os.environ["FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_LIVE_TEST"] = key
    try:
        if sys.argv[1] == "visibility":
            import verify_worker_receipt_visibility

            result = verify_worker_receipt_visibility.run(key=key)
        elif sys.argv[1] == "failover":

        return 0 if result["status"] == "passed" else 1
    finally:
        os.environ.pop("FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_LIVE_TEST", None)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Optional HTTP-attempt ceiling uses the existing durable admission transaction."""

import sqlite3
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from threading import Barrier

import pytest

from forge_core.model_budget_schema import migrate_model_budget
from forge_core.model_call_budget import BudgetExceeded, ModelCallBudgetLedger
from forge_core.runtime import ModelCallContext


def ledger(path, limit):
    return ModelCallBudgetLedger(
        path, token_limit=1000, concurrency_limit=4, call_limit=limit, remote_max_seconds=30
    )


def admit(budget, key):
    return budget.admit(
        ModelCallContext(key, "router", "workspace"),
        "provider",
        "model",
        input_tokens=4,
        output_tokens=4,
        remote_timeout=30,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [0, -1, True, 1.5, "2"])
def test_invalid_call_ceiling_rejected(tmp_path, value):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="call limit"):
        ledger(tmp_path / "budget.sqlite", value)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("outcome", ["settled", "unknown", "rejected", "reserved"])
def test_attempt_ceiling_survives_settlement_and_reopening(tmp_path, outcome):
    path = tmp_path / "budget.sqlite"
    with sqlite3.connect(path) as connection:
        migrate_model_budget(connection)
    budget = ledger(path, 1)
    attempt = admit(budget, "first")
    if outcome == "settled":
        budget.settle(attempt, {"input_tokens": 2, "output_tokens": 1})
    elif outcome == "unknown":
        budget.settle(attempt, {"input_tokens": None, "output_tokens": None})
    elif outcome == "rejected":
        budget.reject_completed(attempt)
    with pytest.raises(BudgetExceeded, match="call limit exhausted"):
        admit(ledger(path, 1), "after_restart")
    with sqlite3.connect(path) as connection:
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_budget_attempts").fetchone()[0] == 1


def test_competing_admissions_cannot_exceed_one_remaining_call(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "budget.sqlite"
    with sqlite3.connect(path) as connection:
        migrate_model_budget(connection)
    barrier = Barrier(2)

    def compete(key):
        budget = ledger(path, 1)
        barrier.wait(timeout=5)
        try:
            admit(budget, key)
            return "admitted"
        except BudgetExceeded:
            return "denied"

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(compete, str(index)) for index in range(2)]
        assert sorted(item.result(timeout=10) for item in futures) == ["admitted", "denied"]
    with sqlite3.connect(path) as connection:
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_budget_attempts").fetchone()[0] == 1

def test_attempt_ceiling_survives_settlement_and_reopening(tmp_path, outcome):
    path = tmp_path / "budget.sqlite"
    with sqlite3.connect(path) as connection:

def test_competing_admissions_cannot_exceed_one_remaining_call(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "budget.sqlite"
    with sqlite3.connect(path) as connection:
        migrate_model_budget(connection)
    barrier = Barrier(2)

    def compete(key):
        budget = ledger(path, 1)
        barrier.wait(timeout=5)
        try:
            admit(budget, key)
            return "admitted"
        except BudgetExceeded:
            return "denied"

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(compete, str(index)) for index in range(2)]
        assert sorted(item.result(timeout=10) for item in futures) == ["admitted", "denied"]

def _ratio(passed, total):
    return {"passed": passed, "samples": total, "value": passed / total if total else None}


def read_metrics(database):
    """Read one consistent SQLite snapshot without creating/migrating the DB.

    A Core state of completed and receipt hash integrity are observations, not
    an independent task-content oracle. Gateway attempt rows have no live/mock
    column: non-Worker call provenance therefore remains explicitly unattributed.
    """
    path = Path(database).resolve()
    if not path.is_file():
        raise ValueError("Metrics database must already exist")

        c.row_factory = sqlite3.Row

        runs = rows("SELECT id,quest_id,worker_id,state,execution_mode,repairs FROM worker_runs ORDER BY id")

        subscriptions = c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superagent_subscriptions").fetchone()[0]
        deliveries = c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superagent_trigger_deliveries").fetchone()[0]
    by_run = {row["id"]: row for row in runs}
    known_usage = [row for row in calls if row["input_charged"] is not None and row["output_charged"] is not None]
    currencies = {row["currency"] for row in calls}
    cost_known = bool(calls) and all(row["cost_charged"] is not None for row in calls) and len(currencies) == 1 and None not in currencies
